limitations: Concept-only review; no game, native-grid, animation, collision, engineering, flood or physical-safety validation.
Static props do not prove completed rescue, payments, crop ownership, consent, proxy authorization or actual access rights.

findings.finding: Stopped-looking rope wheel is behind railing, with cloth strips and an EMPTY staged stretcher; no trapped/rescued people or completed rescue are depicted. Public foreground bypass stays outside mine equipment. Right withdrawal room has independent access, but its right-side exit visibly uses several stone STEPS, not the required gentle solid dry ramp in FOR-D01. Replace that stepped route with a visibly continuous ground ramp before treating accessible withdrawal as resolved. Front yard path remains open, so this is not a claim all exits are blocked. Empty tags and pouch do not prove anyone has exited, been paid or consented to work. Professional rescue must continue independently of wage/institutional decisions; unconfirmed people stay pending, and new survivor dialogue requires actual exit and voluntary presence.

Two scales and separate coarse/fine ore bins are visible behind the low dust wall. Clean accounting room has a distinct street opening and separate compartments for tokens and two tied bags. However, the share tokens render as circular ochre/gold-colored disks with coin-like rim/face marks. Their intended wood material is not visually unambiguous. Replace them with clearly rectangular notched wooden share tallies, leaving wage and water-payment pouches separate; do not rely on a caption to reinterpret apparent coins. Source explicitly says unredeemed mine shares are not paid base wages, and the same pool cannot cover wages, inspection and water twice. No exchange is shown, so image does not prove payment. Repeated-deduction notch evidence remains too weak for a final investigation prop.

Fan housing is enclosed by slats and separated from external walkway by a rail. Two cloth strips, detached clogged screen and an independently placed lever are visible; separate discussion shelter opens to its own public approach. Static image cannot prove the fan is stopped, safe airflow, lever linkage or acceptance testing. Fee pouch and wage tallies are separate categories, not funds already received. Keep conservative closure/ongoing rescue independent of discussion and do not imply injured workers must re-enter or disclose full medical histories.

A single old cup and separate empty stand occupy the left cabinet; cup motif is generic and does not authenticate a present-day military office. Right proxy room has unmistakable narrow wooden tallies, closed folio, blank period board and empty chair. Two rooms have separate open entries to common dry path; no forced route through cup display. Nearby barrels and containers narrow internal clearance and require scaled layout. Cup display, inherited share, limited proxy and new labor consent remain separate; no signed agreement or cash receipt appears.

Compared with original 92 inspected in the preceding pass: a new visible stone stair runs beside the LEFT weighing shelter from low-quay vicinity to the high embankment, resolving the previously missing depicted dry return connection at concept level. Stair continues above the high path toward forest, an unrequested extension, and the bottom landing is narrow/partly screened by the mooring post. Validate an explicit unobstructed lower landing, high-path junction, handrails, elevations and flood closure in scaled layout; do not claim exact navigation proven. Right home stays intact and detached beams remain separate. Neither raft, beam rack nor refund token establishes all-resident consent, actual safe relocation, payment or load capacity. Broad arrangement is retained, not pixel-exact preservation.

overall: 92 v2 supplies the missing depicted dry stair with remaining clearance limits. Correct 95 stepped withdrawal exit to ramp and 96 coin-like share tokens to clearly wooden tallies. Rescue and all finance/consent outcomes remain unproven.
